strings.URP_king_without_country_desc:
The López family in the 19th century and Morínigo in the 20th secured near-absolute power over Paraguay for themselves. How far their successors have fallen.

Orders and laws emanating from the Palacio de los López and the Palacio Legislativo reach only to the city limits of Asunción. Beyond that, they take force only according to the whims of Brazilian or Argentinian military authorities.

And within those circumscribed boundaries, fervid lustration has left the city bereft of senior officials and the failures of the war effort have cleansed it of junior ones. The only remaining force capable of action are OAS peacekeepers. Who are, of course, unbound from any Paraguayan authority.
strings.URP_duel_marionettes_desc:
Every strand of Paraguayan thought has found expression in the new provisional government. But this inclusivity matters little given the puppet strings attached.

Behind the thin curtain of the OAS framework, Brasília and Buenos Aires direct opposing factions of collaborators through a host of intrigues and squabbles. The stage directions occasionally referenced by American states further afield are roundly ignored as both powers slice at the ties that bind Asunción to their rival.

And the Paraguayan citizenry playing audience to this farce? Entangled, yes. Enraged, certainly. Entertained? Assuredly not.
strings.URP_reascension_desc:
The fields where soybeans, manioc, and cotton once grew lie fallow. The sounds of harps grow faint. The appearance of a police officer or mail carrier now counts for a luxury.

And that is the state of Paraguay beyond Asunción, the devastated epicenter of civil and foreign wars. The rubble has not been cleared from Palacio de los López, much less from the streets. Power is intermittent at best, and damage to the sewage system has raised fears of disease. The many hungry roam the city, hunting for the trickle of aid the OAS brings in on battered roads or a donated half-ration from a peacekeeper. Yet even those scraps offer greater relief than another empty proclamation from their own government.
